How High Alchemy Works

High Level Alchemy is a level 55 Magic spell on the standard spellbook. Each cast requires 1 nature rune and 5 fire runes — though you should always equip a fire staff or tome of fire to eliminate the fire rune cost entirely. The spell converts any tradeable item into gold coins equal to 60% of its store price, a fixed value known as the "high alch value."

You can cast approximately 1,200 alchs per hour at maximum speed. The profit formula for each cast is straightforward: Alch Value - Buy Price - Nature Rune Cost = Profit. Any item whose high alch value exceeds the sum of its current GE buy price and the cost of a nature rune is profitable to alch. The tables below show exactly which items meet that criteria right now.

The key to consistent alch profits is using live price data rather than outdated lists. Item prices fluctuate constantly on the Grand Exchange, and an item that was profitable yesterday might be a loss today. Use the High Alch Calculator to search and sort every alchable item with real-time pricing.

Best Item Categories for Alching

Rune equipment is the classic alching staple. Items like rune platebodies, rune platelegs, and rune kiteshields have high alch values and consistent supply from PvM drops. Their buy limits are generous enough to sustain extended alching sessions, making them a reliable default choice.

Dragon items such as dragon longswords and dragon daggers offer higher profit per cast but come with more price volatility. Jewelry and enchanted items are frequently overlooked — rings, necklaces, and amulets can be surprisingly profitable when demand dips. Crafted items like battlestaves and dragonhide bodies benefit from steady supply via skillers, keeping prices predictable.

Each category carries a different risk profile. Rune items are stable but competitive; dragon items fluctuate more but reward timing. Diversify across categories to stay profitable even when one market shifts. Browse all item categories in the item database to find alchable items by sector.

Alching vs Flipping: When to Use Each Method

Alching is a passive money-making method — you can cast it while training agility on rooftop courses, grinding slayer tasks, or doing quests. This makes it ideal for players who want to earn GP without dedicating full attention to the Grand Exchange. Flipping, on the other hand, requires active management of buy and sell offers but can be done largely AFK between offer checks.

Alching has a hard GP/hour ceiling determined by nature rune prices and item buy limits. No matter how good the items are, you're capped at around 1,200 casts per hour. Flipping scales with your bank — more capital means more simultaneous offers and higher total profit. A player with 100M GP flipping across all 8 GE slots will vastly out-earn any alching session.

The best strategy is to combine both methods. Buy items to alch from the GE while your flip offers are filling in the background. This keeps your gold productive at all times — you're never just waiting. Alching excels at consistent, low-effort income, while flipping is better for aggressive wealth growth. Learn more in our Flipping Guide for Beginners or find budget flip opportunities in the Low Capital Flips Guide.

How to Maximize Alch Profits

  • 1.Always check live prices before bulk buying. An item profitable 30 minutes ago may have shifted. This page updates every 10 minutes.
  • 2.Watch buy limits — you can only buy a fixed number of each item per 4 hours. Diversify across multiple items to keep alching.
  • 3.Alch while doing other activities (agility, slayer) to train Magic passively. Use a nature rune staff to save fire runes.
  • 4.Consider flipping alongside alching — buy items to alch from the GE while your flip offers fill. See our Low Capital Flipping Guide for ideas.
  • 5.Track your alch profits over time with the Profit Tracker to see your daily and weekly earnings.

Nature Rune Cost

Nature runes currently cost 147 GP each on the Grand Exchange. This price directly impacts which items are profitable to alch — when nature runes are cheap, more items become worthwhile. Track the live price on the nature rune item page.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best item to high alch in OSRS?

The best high alch item changes constantly with GE prices. Right now, the top item yields 2,694 GP profit per cast. Check the tables above for live data — they update every 10 minutes.

Is high alching profitable in 2026?

Yes. With nature runes currently at 147 GP, there are 151 items that are profitable to alch right now. The key is using live data to find items where the alch value exceeds the buy price plus nature rune cost.

How many high alchs can you do per hour?

You can cast approximately 1,200 high alchs per hour. However, your actual GP/hour depends on buy limits — if an item has a buy limit of 100, you can only alch 100 per 4 hours. The GP/Hour column factors in buy limits.
